findings.title: TOCTOU race allows exceeding device limit
findings.body: In CreateOrUpdateDevice, the device count is read in one DB session (s.CountDevices) and the subsequent INSERT/UPDATE runs in a separate session. Under concurrent load, multiple requests can all observe count < limit and all proceed to INSERT, allowing the actual device count to exceed the configured limit by the number of in-flight requests. The check-then-act must be wrapped in a transaction with appropriate locking, or the limit enforced by a DB-level mechanism, to guarantee the cap.

findings.title: TagDevice moved to synchronous request context
findings.body: The previous implementation called TagDevice in a goroutine with an independent 2-minute context (context.Background() + WithTimeout). The new code calls TagDevice synchronously using the request context. Consequences: (a) every anonymous auth now pays the full DB latency (count + insert/update) on the hot path; (b) if the client cancels the request, the request context is cancelled and the device is never tagged, which both skews the usage stat 'stats.anonymous.device.ui.count' and lets a device avoid being counted against the limit. The async design should be retained for non-limit errors and only the limit-exceeded path needs to surface synchronously.

findings.title: Extra COUNT(*) on every anonymous auth when limit is set
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice now issues a SELECT COUNT(*) ... WHERE updated_at BETWEEN ... AND ... on every call when deviceLimit > 0. There is no caching of the count and the check runs unconditionally on the auth hot path, adding a full table scan (or index scan) to every anonymous request even when the limit is nowhere near being reached.

findings.title: Auth-flow behavior change for ErrDeviceLimitReached has no test
findings.body: Anonymous.Authenticate now propagates anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached up so authentication fails when the limit is hit. The new integration test (TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit) only covers the store-level CreateOrUpdateDevice path; there is no test that exercises Anonymous.Authenticate to confirm (1) ErrDeviceLimitReached causes Authenticate to return an error rather than a successful identity, and (2) other errors from TagDevice are still swallowed with a warning. This is a behavior change that warrants a dedicated test, including asserting what HTTP status / message a real request would receive.

findings.title: New device_limit setting has no user-facing documentation
findings.body: The PR adds cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit read from [auth.anonymous] device_limit with default 0 (treated as unlimited), but no documentation file (e.g. docs/sources/setup-grafana/configure-grafana/_index.md or similar) is updated. Operators have no way to learn about the new key, its semantics (0 = unlimited, what happens at the limit, interaction with the 30-day cleanup window), or its env-var override name (expected GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT). The default sentinel of 0 and the rejection semantics (new devices rejected, existing devices continue to update) also need to be called out.

findings.title: updateDevice query does not handle new vs expired-device distinction
findings.body: When count >= deviceLimit the code routes to updateDevice, whose WHERE clause requires updated_at BETWEEN device.UpdatedAt-30d AND device.UpdatedAt+1m. A row that exists but whose updated_at is older than 30 days (still within the 61-day cleanup window) will be reported as 'no rows affected' and surface ErrDeviceLimitReached, indistinguishable from a genuinely new device. The caller cannot tell whether to retry later (e.g. after cleanup) or give up. Either the WHERE should also match such rows so they get refreshed, or the error should distinguish 'limit reached' from 'device expired/not found'.
